prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer's own torso and shoulders at the bottom of the frame are brightest and nearest (0.1 to 0.4 metres below the head-mounted camera), facing forward in the direction of travel with no other people present. Directly in front of the torso and within arm's reach, the wearer's extended forearms and hands grip a lawnmower handlebar at roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres away, while the mower's grass catcher bag and engine deck sit further ahead and lower down at approximately 0.8 to 1.5 metres above the dark background ground plane (around 1.5 to 2.0 metres below the camera). In frames 1 and 2, medium-bright foliage from a bush appears on the right edge at roughly 1.0 to 1.3 metres from the camera and 0.4 metres to the right of the mower, whereas in frames 1 through 3 the front of the mower is partially cut off by the top edge of the frame and the wearer's shirt occludes their feet except for brief glimpses under the handlebar in frames 2 and 3. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer walks forward along a grassy strip bordered by a concrete walkway on the left, approaching the end of the lawn strip and turning slightly left in frames 4 and 5 so the full mower deck enters the top-right of the view and a raised white curb/step edge becomes visible on the left. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the raised mower handlebar, side struts, and protruding right-hand bush foliage from the flat grass below, though it looks unreliable along the flat walkway where high-contrast concrete seams and shadows in frames 4 and 5 create false depth discontinuities.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower body, torso, and arms at the bottom of all 5 frames as a foreground 'person' mask positioned 0.1 to 0.7 metres below and in front of the camera, facing forward away from the camera lens with no other people in the scene. Within the wearer's arm's reach at roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres in front of the chest, the map outlines the central grip of the lawnmower handlebar in frames 1 and 3, while the mower's main body sits 0.3 to 0.8 metres further ahead in front of the hands. Across the 5 frames, as the wearer walks forward and angles left in frames 4 and 5, the foreground torso mask shifts slightly toward the bottom-right and the distant mower mask shifts toward the upper-right as more of the front mower deck comes into view after being partially cut off at the top of frames 1 to 3. The segmentation map clearly delineates the continuous silhouette of the wearer's shirt and arms against the ground and highlights the small gaps between the forearms, chest, and handlebar where the grass and occluded feet lie below, which is harder to isolate at a glance in the textured RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labeling and object completeness: it completely misses the lawnmower, walkway, and bushes, misclassifies the mower handlebar grip as a 'cell phone' in frames 1 and 3, and falsely labels the lawnmower's red engine cap and grass catcher bag at 0.8 to 1.5 metres ahead as a second 'person' in frames 3, 4, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map detects only two magenta hand skeletons in front of the camera wearer at roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres distance and separated from each other by about 0.35 to 0.4 metres horizontally, with no yellow body skeletons and no other people present in the scene. The left and right hands are positioned symmetrically to the left and right of the frame center, below and in front of the wearer's head, oriented forward and downward as the fingers curl around the lawnmower handlebar within immediate arm's reach. Because the egocentric camera looks straight down over the wearer's chest, the head and lower body are out of view or self-occluded by the green shirt, leaving only the outstretched arms and hands visible above the ground. Across frames 1 to 3, the pair of hand skeletons stays at a steady height and spacing as the wearer walks straight ahead, then shifts downward in frame 4 and angles down and to the right in frame 5 as the wearer turns slightly left near the end of the lawn strip. While the pose map makes the exact finger joint articulation, thumb orientation, and grip posture on the handlebar much easier to see than in the small RGB frames, it is unreliable in missing the wearer's shoulders and elbows entirely across all frames and failing to detect the right hand skeleton in frame 5 even though that hand remains clearly visible on the handlebar.
